issues.title: fix: preserve cancellation in dialog light-dismiss fallback

labels.name: content
labels.description: Pertaining to what the guidance instructs

issues.body:
Backdrop dismissal in the light-dismiss fallback calls `close()` directly, bypassing `cancel` handlers that prevent dismissal. This reproduces in Chromium 131 and WebKit 26.5: Escape respects a guard, but clicking the backdrop closes the dialog.

Dispatch a cancelable `cancel` event before closing, and clarify that `close` handlers run after dismissal. Replace the grader's source-string fallback check with behavior checks, including cancellation. Related to #1671; this narrowly addresses cancellation, leaving its drag-selection and cross-guide fallback-policy questions open.

Validation: the demo passes all 9 grader checks; the original fails the cancellation check, a comment-only fallback fails both fallback checks, and a working `requestClose()` alternative passes. The negative demo fails all 9 checks. Real-browser before/after checks passed in Chromium 131 and WebKit 26.5, with native behavior checked in Chromium 149.

Build, typecheck, lint, and 28 focused integrity/static checks pass. Full preflight is not green: guide validation has seven coverage failures reproduced on untouched `5e5cd33`; other failures involve missing shallow-clone history/tags, a model-download timeout, Node/Astro version compatibility, and process teardown. Historical replay requires renewed GCS authentication.

<!-- mwg-demo-preview:start -->
---

issues.title: fix: resolve custom command fallback targets in the button's tree

labels.name: content
labels.description: Pertaining to what the guidance instructs

issues.body:
The manual custom-command fallback finds buttons through `composedPath()`, including buttons inside open shadow roots, but resolves their targets through `document.getElementById()`. A shadow-local target is therefore missed; if the document contains the same ID, the fallback sends the command to that unrelated element instead. Resolve the target through `button.getRootNode()` and clarify the existing same-tree constraint. This follows the [HTML commandfor targeting rule](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-button-commandfor). The change is confined to the manual fallback in `guide.md`; the demo uses the separately recommended invokers-polyfill. ### Reproduction Before installing the guide's manual fallback, set up this fixture and click Run: ```js document.body.innerHTML = '
'; const root = document.getElementById('host').attachShadow({mode: 'open'}); root.innerHTML = `
`; document.getElementById('target').addEventListener('command', () => console.log('outside')); root.getElementById('target').addEventListener('command', () => console.log('inside')); ``` In Chromium 131 (without native invoker commands), the original fallback logs `outside`; the patched snippet logs `inside`, matching native Chromium 149. Removing the shadow target should dispatch no command, but the original fallback still activates the outside element. ### Validation Browser checks exercised the extracted guide snippet via HTTP and real clicks on a child span in each button. All four cases pass after the fix in Chromium 131.0.6778.33 and native Chromium 149.0.7827.55: document target, shadow-local target, duplicate ID outside the shadow root, and missing shadow-local target. The original fallback fails the last three; command values and source buttons were also checked. `pnpm build` passes. Guide integrity reports 841 passing tests and seven pre-existing expectation-coverage failures in unrelated guides (translator, drag, spatial-navigation, swipe-to-reveal, carousel, checkbox, spinner); this guide's validation, Markdown, and macro checks pass. Full `pnpm preflight` also completes build, typecheck, and lint (two existing warnings), then fails in the test stage. Besides the coverage failures above, local failures involve shallow-history/release-baseline assumptions, date-sensitive eval expectations, child-server teardown, and the base app requiring a newer Node patch version than the installed 22.23.2. These same categories were observed on the unchanged upstream base during the preceding investigation; this is not a claim that full preflight is green.

issues.title: fix(legacy-scan): expose max-files option
issues.body:
Refs #3596

## Problem

`legacy-scan` collects at most 5,000 eligible source files (`scanRepoFiles`' `maxFiles` default). `runAnalyzeCli` already accepts a programmatic `maxFiles` option, but the CLI has no flag for it, so CLI users cannot scan past the cap.

Reproduction on `main` (`5e5cd33`), using a git repo with 5,000 clean CSS files plus `src/zz-last.css` containing `.box::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`, scanned with `--json --guide customize-scrollbar-color-and-thickness`:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Default CLI | 0 findings (the last file is never collected) |
| `runAnalyzeCli(args, { maxFiles: 5001 })` | 1 finding |
| Direct scan of `src/zz-last.css` | 1 finding |
| `--max-files 5001` | exit 1, `Unknown option '--max-files'` |

## Change

- `src/analyzing/cli.ts`: add a `--max-files <count>` string option to `legacy-scan` / `analyze`, with a help row. The value must be ASCII decimal digits forming a positive safe integer (leading zeros allowed, so `0002` is 2). Zero, signs, fractions, exponents, hex, whitespace, empty values and values above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are rejected through the existing human/JSON error path with exit code 1. This check runs before any filesystem access. Missing values, repeated flags and unknown flags keep the existing `parseArgs` behavior. The parse-error target heuristic now skips the value after `--max-files`, as it already does for `--guide` and `--skill-version`, so `--max-files 2 project --unknown --json` reports target `project`.
- Precedence: **explicit `--max-files` → existing `options.maxFiles` → scanner default 5,000.** The programmatic option stays a fallback, not a ceiling, and its validation is unchanged.
- The cap keeps its current meaning (eligible source files collected by the scanner). Single-file targets, findings, JSON shape and exit codes are unchanged. No truncation warning or counters are added. Diagnostics are left to the separate discussion in #3587.
- `bin/gd.ts`: add the flag to `ALL_OPTIONS` and `legacy-scan` metadata so `gd --help` and shell completion list it.
- `src/analyzing/README.md`: add an options-table row and one larger-repository example.

The scanner, the public wrapper (`src/cli/modern-web.ts`, which already forwards raw arguments), dependencies and shared configs are unchanged.

## Tests

New tests in `src/analyzing/cli.test.ts` use a three-file temp directory and a test-local CSS rule:

- Flag cases: no flag gives 3 findings, `--max-files 1` gives 1, `--max-files=2` gives 2, and `--max-files 0002` gives 2.
- Precedence: `options.maxFiles=1` alone gives 1. Adding `--max-files 2` gives 2.
- An explicit single-file target with `--max-files 1` still returns its finding.
- Invalid values (`0`, `=-1`, `1.5`, `abc`, `9007199254740992`, `1e3`, `0x10`, `+1`, ` 1`, and an empty `=` value) are each checked against a nonexistent target. The human path writes to stderr with an empty stdout. The JSON path stays parseable on stdout, keeps the target, and returns empty findings/guides with an `error`. Neither path reaches the "Target path not found" check.
- A missing value goes through `parseArgs`.
- Help includes `--max-files <count>`, and the parse-error target case is covered.

`src/cli/modern-web.test.ts` has one public-wrapper test: `legacy-scan <dir> --json` gives 3 findings and `--max-files 1` gives 1.

The new tests failed on unchanged code because of `Unknown option '--max-files'`.

Results (local, Node 24.22.1 as in CI, pnpm 10.30.3):

- `node --test src/analyzing/cli.test.ts src/cli/modern-web.test.ts`: 35 passed, 0 failed (baseline was 18 + 12)
- `node --test src/analyzing/scanners/scanners.test.ts`: 71 passed, 0 failed (covers `maxFiles=70` across 64-file read batches)
- `pnpm typecheck`: pass
- `pnpm lint`: 0 errors, 2 warnings (both pre-existing, in `guides/ui-atoms/single-line-overflow/targets/daily-grind/grader.ts`)
- `pnpm preflight`: build, typecheck and lint pass. Tests: 3190 total, 3177 passed, 9 skipped, **4 failed**. The same 4 tests fail on unchanged `main` locally (3185 total, 3172 passed, 4 failed, 9 skipped), all in `src/ci/sync-pipeline-issue.test.ts`. Three depend on the timezone (they pass with `TZ=UTC`; my machine is UTC+7). One (`includes discipline guides in all counts and the progress bar`) fails in every timezone on unchanged code and appears to depend on the current date. CI on `main` passed at `5e5cd33`. This PR does not touch that area.
- One-off integration check, outside the repo and not committed: the 5,001-file fixture above through both `runAnalyzeCli` and `node src/cli/modern-web.ts legacy-scan`. The default still finds 0. `--max-files 5001` finds 1, including when `options.maxFiles=5000` is also set. The direct-file control finds 1.

The build left the working tree clean, and no generated or lockfile changes are included.

## Contributor checklist

- [ ] Google CLA: **not yet verified** for this contributor (pqminh27). This must be confirmed before merge, so the PR is opened as a draft.
- [x] Focused on one change (flag only). Issue #3596 also asks for truncation reporting, which is out of scope here, so this uses `Refs` rather than `Fixes`.
- [x] No changes to root `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`, `.oxlintignore` or lockfile.

issues.title: cli(retrieve): suggest similar guide IDs and accept path-like IDs
issues.body:
## Summary

When an agent guesses or mistypes a guide ID, `retrieve` prints the raw error with a multi-line stack trace and no help:

```
$ npx modern-web-guidance retrieve optimise-image-priority
Retrieve failed for optimise-image-priority: Error: No guide found …
    at retrieveUseCase (…)
    … (7 stack lines)
```

Path-shaped IDs such as `performance/optimize-image-priority` or `optimize-image-priority.md` are also rejected.

## Change

- `src/rag/guide-ids.ts` (new, dependency-free): `normalizeGuideId` (case-insensitive; strips an optional `guides/<category>/` or `<category>/` prefix and a `.md` / `/guide.md` suffix) and `suggestGuideIds` (≤ 3 suggestions, ranked by optimal-string-alignment edit similarity combined with word overlap, thresholded so unrelated input gets none).
- `retrieve.ts`: `UnknownGuideError` carries the suggestions; `formatUnknownGuideMessage` keeps the message to two lines with the echoed ID truncated to 80 chars:
  ```
  Unknown guide ID "optimise-image-priority". Did you mean: optimize-image-priority?
  Use `npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "<query>"` to find guides.
  ```
- `modern-web.ts`: flags are filtered, then IDs are normalized and de-duplicated before lookup; `UnknownGuideError` prints without a stack trace. Valid guides requested alongside an unknown ID are still printed, and the command exits 1. IDs that normalize to empty (`/`, `.md`) are reported as unknown rather than "No IDs provided".

Output for valid IDs and the origin-trial / volatile feature-gate behaviour are unchanged. The "guide listed but markdown missing" path still throws with its stack, since that is a packaging bug rather than a user typo.

## Testing

- `guide-ids.test.ts`: normalization, edit distance, ranking (typos, transpositions, partial IDs, extra/missing words, threshold boundary, cap of 3, garbage, empty candidate list).
- `retrieve.test.ts`: `UnknownGuideError` suggestions and truncation.
- `modern-web.test.ts`: tolerant spellings give byte-identical output; mixed valid + unknown; empty-normalizing IDs; long IDs.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` pass.
